title: The Ridge's Memory Grove

features.name: the-path-of-repeated-choosing
features.desc-on-touch: Footprints worn into stone. You see each moment marked—every body that believed they chose, and was chosen by the land.

features.name: cairn-of-the-still-choosing
features.desc-on-touch: Stones stacked by every hand that came here. You touch their warmth—some are old, some were placed yesterday.

features.name: the-choice-voice
features.desc-on-touch: The ridge hums with every path taken. Listen, and you hear which directions people chose most, and which they resisted.

features.name: the-memory-wind
features.desc-on-touch: The breeze carries dust from a hundred years of walking. You smell soil from paths not yet taken.

features.name: the-stone-that-chose-itself
features.desc-on-touch: This stone sits alone at the summit. You feel the weight it holds: the record of all choosing below.

inscription: every moment of choosing is a stone the ridge remembers; you are the echo of a footstep not yet taken

file.name: Ridge_NSW_ChoiceStones_Photograph_1987.png
file.note: A hiker's Polaroid of the ridge at sunset. The image ages backward, showing footprints that haven't walked yet.

reverie.title: REVERIE — ridge at dusk
narr: You stand at the highest point. She's pointing at the
worn stone, tracing the oldest footprints with one hand.
The ridge shows you both the history of every step. But
below those old feet, the stone is still waiting. Still
choosing what to remember. She takes your hand. You both
know the choice was made long before either of you arrived.

exits.label: back down the ridge toward the choice-stones you remember
further into the grove where the oldest stones forget whose feet walked them
upward to the summit where all chosen paths arrive at once
down into the memory-valley where unchosen paths dream of being walked
